newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian central bank cuts interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Australian central bank cuts interest rates.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) on Wednesday cut official interest rates by 0.5 percentage points to 5.0 percent, citing a favourable inflation performance and scope for faster economic growth.
The cut is the fifth reduction in official cash rates in a year.

"This change, like the four previous reductions in interest rates over the past year, is based on the improving picture for Australia's medium-term inflation performance, which opens up scope for faster growth and employment," the central bank said.
The RBA said in the year to June the underlying rate of inflation was 1.7 percent and that it expected underlying inflation to stay below 2.0 percent into 1998.
The bank said economic growth in 1997 had been picking up, but remained moderate. Economic growth was an annual 2.4 percent in the March quarter and unemployment was at 8.5 percent in June.
"The crucial test for monetary policy is to have the setting that will best contribute to low inflation and economic growth in the long run," it said.
